![Three people in a financial services conference room with video meeting on screen](https://avispl.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Three-people-in-a-financial-services-conference-room-with-video-meeting-on-screen.jpg)

A client conversation can influence how a small business funds its next stage of growth. For an individual, a financial discussion can shape how they provide for their family or prepare for retirement. Employees also work with large volumes of company and client information as they make decisions that affect how the organization operates. All of this happens in your collaboration spaces every day.

For CIOs, the challenge is meeting the needs of both clients and employees while giving your IT team a collaboration environment it can protect and support. The experience should feel intuitive for the people in the room and familiar as employees move among spaces and locations. A balanced approach brings those requirements together, so the technology reinforces the professional standards clients expect from the organization.

## Start with security

The first consideration is security. Clients and employees need confidence that the conversations and information shared in a collaboration space are protected. In financial services, privacy and regulatory requirements raise that expectation further, so security needs to influence how the room is planned from the beginning.

Room planning gives your IT team an opportunity to make those protections intentional. Teams need to know which platforms and endpoints are approved before deciding what belongs in the space. Access also has to reflect the controls your organization already uses. Making these decisions during design helps IT build security into how the room operates instead of trying to solve for it after deployment.

The room also must support people who attend meetings remotely. A client may join from home while an employee connects from another office, yet both are participating in the same financial conversation. The same privacy and security requirements apply wherever participants connect.

Some complexity is unavoidable when IT is protecting a growing collaboration environment. The challenge is controlling that complexity, so security remains practical to administer as rooms and requirements change. Participants should not have to work through those security layers every time they meet. From their perspective, the room still needs to be straightforward to use.

## Make the meeting easy

A room can meet every security requirement and the experience may still fall short for the people using it. A client walking into a space for the first time should not need a tutorial before the meeting can begin. Employees should not have to call for help with routine tasks. The room should make it easy for people with different levels of technical comfort to start or join a meeting.

A financial advisor may move from discussing a client’s goals to reviewing a plan on screen. An internal team may bring confidential growth strategies into the discussion before deciding how to move forward. In both cases, people need to see and understand the information in front of them without having to think about the room itself. Sharing content should feel like part of the meeting, not a separate task someone has to stop and manage.

#### Bring information into view with Planar

Financial conversations often depend on making complex information easier to see and understand. Strong visuals can give everyone a shared view of performance data or plans while helping presenters explain the story behind the numbers. [Planar](https://avispl.com/Planar/) large-format LCD displays support visual communication in collaboration spaces and corporate lobbies, with touch and non-touch options suited to how each environment is used.

##### Support visual communication across financial spacess

- Work directly with information using Planar UltraRes P Series touch displays, with 50-point touch models supporting annotation and whiteboarding during collaborative discussions.
- Present detailed dashboards and reports on UltraRes P Series 4K displays, with high brightness supporting clear viewing of detailed content.
- When interaction is not required, choose non-touch models for spaces where the display serves as a shared visual reference throughout the discussion.
- Extend visual communication into corporate lobbies with Planar Simplicity P Series 4K displays, designed for digital signage and continuous commercial operation.
- Support cybersecurity priorities with UltraRes P Series displays certified to ETSI EN 303 645, helping mitigate security threats in connected environments.

[Learn more about Planar](https://avispl.com/planar/)

![: Instructor using a Planar large-format display to present visual course content to students in a higher education classroom.](https://avispl.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Planar-Corporate_Touch-LCD.png)

Remote attendees should have the same opportunity to take part as everyone else. For that to happen, they need to hear and be heard clearly enough to stay in the conversation. They should be able to follow the discussion and speak up when it matters instead of feeling like an observer looking into the room.

A good experience in one room shapes what people expect from the next. The question for you is how to preserve that experience as collaboration extends beyond a single space.

## Create consistency across spaces

Different rooms can support different kinds of work and still keep the basic meeting experience familiar. Employees should not have to relearn how to start or run a meeting each time they move to another space. Consistency comes from deciding what should stay familiar even when the space itself is designed for a different purpose.

Standardization gives IT a common foundation for how collaboration spaces operate. During planning, teams can define the platform and core control approach that carries from room to room. They can then decide where a particular use case calls for something different.

This gives IT a clear reference point for technology choices beyond core elements. Additional technology can be selected for the work taking place without changing the elements IT has chosen to standardize.

The same approach also gives IT fewer exceptions to carry forward. When every room is treated as its own project, each new space adds unique configurations and support requirements the technology team must manage. ~~~~

Standards give your IT leaders a known starting point when a new office opens or an existing space is refreshed. Teams can account for new requirements within that framework instead of reopening the same basic decisions with every project.

#### Simplify Room Audio and Video with Jabra

As financial organizations equip more meeting spaces, video bars offer an integrated way to support room audio and video. By bringing the camera, microphones and speaker together in one device, they reduce the number of separate components IT has to deploy and support. [Jabra](https://avispl.com/jabra/) PanaCast U30 brings that approach to smaller meeting rooms, providing the in-room audio and video while employees connect their own laptop and use a familiar meeting platform.

##### Equip Smaller Financial Spaces for Hybrid Meetings

- Use familiar platforms such as Microsoft Teams or Zoom from an employee’s own laptop, connecting to the room with a single USB-C cable instead of relying on a dedicated room controller.
- Keep people around the table in view with 4K video, a 120° horizontal field of view and intelligent framing that adjusts to participants in the room.
- Support natural conversation with six microphones and full-duplex audio, while noise suppression and echo cancellation help reduce background distractions.
- Monitor device health, customize settings, and deploy updates remotely through Jabra Plus Management.

[**Tell me more about Jabra**](https://avispl.com/jabra/)

![: Instructor using a Planar large-format display to present visual course content to students in a higher education classroom.](https://avispl.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Small-conference-room-with-Jabra-Reach-with-PanaCast-U30.jpg)

## Balance the meeting experience with IT requirements

The decisions behind a collaboration space are connected. A room that works well for the people using it also has to be manageable for your IT team to protect and support. When both sides inform the design, the room can reflect the professionalism clients expect and give employees a dependable place to do their work.

AVI-SPL helps [financial services organizations](https://avispl.com/industries/financial-services/) plan collaboration technology around the way their people and clients meet today while preparing for changing needs.
